vendors.name: yaml
vendors.knowledge_source: Installed package read 2026-10-12 (yaml 2.9.1, dist/index.d.ts, dist/public-api.d.ts, dist/options.d.ts, dist/errors.d.ts) and the official documentation reference; no Context7 lookup was executed
offline_notes: The advanced YAML editors (naming rules, SPEC section 6; an item's raw properties, SPEC section 3) read and write YAML in the browser, because the wire carries both as typed JSON. The service still validates; the browser is not a second rule engine.

parseDocument records YAML errors and warnings as lists on the Document it returns; parse throws the first recorded error. Show Document.errors at their place (YAMLError.linePos, or pos with a LineCounter) and never send a document that has any.

parseDocument is not promised never to throw: extreme input (very deep nesting) can still end in a RangeError from the call stack, and Document.toJS can throw too. The editor's text is untrusted, so bound its length before parsing, catch whatever is thrown, and show it as one more error; a thrown failure is never read as an empty or valid document. Probed on the installed 2.9.1: 20,000 nested flow sequences were recorded as errors without a throw, which shows the common case, not a guarantee.

What the person typed is untrusted. Keep the defaults that refuse it early: uniqueKeys true (a repeated key is an error), strict true, merge false (no << keys), and the default maxAliasCount bound on alias expansion when a document is turned into values.

A value the wire cannot carry (a date tag, a binary tag, a non-string key, a custom tag) must be refused in plain words, not coerced. Use the core schema of YAML 1.2 (the default), where yes, no, on and off are strings.

Write with compat: 'yaml-1.1': a string that a YAML 1.1 reader would take for a boolean, a number, a date or null (yes, on, 2026-10-12, 1e3, ~) is then quoted, so the text means the same to every reader. Read with it too: an ambiguous plain scalar is then a warning (Document.warnings, code TAG_RESOLVE_FAILED) to show the person; the value stays a string. Probed on the installed 2.9.1. The service's own YAML reader is yaml_serde (crates/storage).

The version option applies only to a document without a %YAML directive: a %YAML 1.1 line in the text turns on merge keys and the 1.1 booleans. Refuse a document that carries a directive (Document.directives) rather than follow it.
stringify keeps the insertion order of an object's keys; do not sort entries, so unknown properties go back in their place.
The package's default export condition for bundlers is ./browser/index.js (ESM); the node condition is CommonJS. It has no dependencies. Licence ISC.
It was already in bun.lock as a transitive dependency of the tooling at 2.9.1; the direct dependency pins the same version.

vendors.name: process-memory-cap
vendors.knowledge_source: Reference notes from reading each pinned crate source downloaded from crates.io (sha256 below); no Context7 lookup was executed (the server was not connected)
offline_notes: One facility per platform behind one cap interface in ingest (verification.json converter-worker-memory-ceiling): Windows a job-object memory limit, Linux RLIMIT_DATA set by the child itself as the first statement of main, macOS a sampling watchdog (owner to confirm it counts as the hard cap). Conversion is never refused on a platform.

processkit 3.3.4 (.crate sha256 1549b59abbe4fc78aa39860e36c81da89262c1278679b8f7299ef4ad7668c004, MIT): ProcessGroup::with_options sets JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_JOB_MEMORY with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (src/sys/windows.rs:491-497); spawn creates the child CREATE_SUSPENDED, assigns it to the job and resumes it (src/sys/windows.rs:636), so no instruction runs outside the cap; stats().peak_memory_bytes is the job PeakJobMemoryUsed (peak committed). Reviewed source of exactly this version: a young crate (first release 2026-05-31) with one maintainer, so any version bump needs a fresh source review. Fallback: process_control 5.2.0, which assigns the job only after the child runs and whose wait cannot kill on drop.

win32job 2.0.3 was rejected: its ExtendedLimitInfo field is pub(crate) and it exposes only limit_working_memory (a working-set limit trims pages and is not a cap). Calling the windows crate directly needs authored unsafe, which AGENTS.md forbids.

rlimit 0.11.0 (.crate sha256 f35ee2729c56bb610f6dba436bf78135f728b7373bdffae2ec815b2d3eb98cc3, MIT): Resource::DATA.set(soft, hard) (src/resource/mod.rs:60). RLIMIT_DATA counts private writable mappings since Linux 4.7 but not PROT_NONE reservations, which ONNX Runtime makes; Resource::AS stays available if the measurement chooses it.

libproc 0.14.11 (macOS only; replaced sysinfo in Batch B): pidrusage::<RUsageInfoV2>(pid) gives ri_phys_footprint, the figure jetsam uses, instead of the resident set. The watchdog kills the child with SIGKILL at the cap minus headroom (at least two sample periods of the worst measured allocation rate, and never less than 5% of the cap). It needs libclang at build time on macOS (bindgen); Windows and Linux builds do not compile it.

Each workos::Jwk is read again as jsonwebtoken::jwk::Jwk through serde, and the accepted algorithms are pinned to RS256.

Features: default off, rust_crypto (ed25519-dalek, hmac, p256, p384, rand, rsa, sha2). The dev-dependency adds use_pem so that tests can sign Connect-shaped tokens with a test-only RSA key (EncodingKey::from_rsa_pem). aws_lc_rs was rejected: aws-lc-sys is a C build that needs NASM, or aws-lc-rs's prebuilt-nasm feature, on Windows x86-64.

The 11.x crypto provider: with exactly one of rust_crypto and aws_lc_rs enabled, the process default is chosen from the features (CryptoProvider::from_crate_features); with both or neither, signing and verifying panic unless CryptoProvider::install_default ran first. Installing crypto::rust_crypto::DEFAULT_PROVIDER at startup keeps verification working if another crate ever enables aws_lc_rs.

rust_crypto pulls rsa 0.9.10, which carries RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin: a timing leak in RSA private-key decryption; no patched release). okf-jawn only verifies signatures with public JWKS keys, so deny.toml and .cargo/audit.toml ignore that one id. Every rsa use stays verify-only, with a comment at the verify site. Remove the ignore when rsa ships a constant-time release or jsonwebtoken moves off it.

vendors.name: tower-http
vendors.knowledge_source: The installed tower-http 0.7.1 source (src/csrf, src/cors, src/services/fs) and docs.rs; no Context7 lookup was run
offline_notes: Batch C (server lane R3) enables fs, cors and csrf for crates/server, behind its runtime feature; qualification/mcp-apps uses cors alone.
fs: ServeDir serves the UI build output, and ServeFile its index fallback.
cors: CorsLayer with an explicit origin list (SPEC section 11, constrained CORS).

csrf: CsrfLayer is the Go 1.25 CrossOriginProtection scheme on Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin (src/csrf/mod.rs). A request passes when its method is GET, HEAD or OPTIONS, when its Origin is a trusted origin (add_trusted_origin), when Sec-Fetch-Site is same-origin or none, when neither header is present, or when the Origin authority equals the request's host; otherwise it is refused with 403. with_rejection_response makes the refusal an ApiError JSON body. It is layered with the double-submit token (contract access::CSRF_COOKIE and CSRF_HEADER), not used instead of it. A proxy that rewrites Host or strips Origin weakens it; forward both unchanged.
tower-http 0.6.11 is also locked, through reqwest; cargo deny warns about the duplicate.
